l4_steps.name: Generate rolling parts demand forecast
l4_steps.input: Scheduled maintenance plan, fleet utilisation forecast, historical consumption rates
l4_steps.output: 12-month rolling parts demand forecast by ATA chapter
l4_steps.kpi: Forecast accuracy ≥85% vs actual consumption over rolling 90-day window
l4_steps.pain_point: Unplanned AOG events and fleet configuration changes (e.g. new aircraft sub-type) invalidate historical consumption rates in AMOS, requiring manual demand model adjustment

l4_steps.name: Calculate reorder points and min/max stock levels
l4_steps.input: Demand forecast, supplier lead times, criticality classification, safety stock policy
l4_steps.output: Updated min/max parameters and reorder point thresholds per part number in AMOS
l4_steps.kpi: Stock-out rate <2% for rotables; <5% for expendables on a rolling 30-day basis
l4_steps.pain_point: Lead time variability from OEM suppliers (Boeing, CFM International) causes chronic stock-out events on critical LRUs; AMOS safety stock calculations do not automatically adjust for supplier performance deviations

l4_steps.name: Classify parts by criticality — AOG, Critical, Routine
l4_steps.input: ATA chapter structure, MEL/CDL requirements, historical AOG event data
l4_steps.output: Part criticality classification list; MEL-linked parts flagged as AOG or Critical in AMOS
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of MEL-linked part numbers classified as AOG or Critical within AMOS
l4_steps.pain_point: MEL revision cycles (typically bi-annual) require manual reclassification in AMOS — no automated sync between regulatory MEL amendments and AMOS part master records

l4_steps.name: Identify approved vendors from Qualified Supplier List
l4_steps.input: Part number, OEM manufacturer P/N, criticality classification, QSL in SAP Ariba
l4_steps.output: Approved vendor shortlist with lead times, pricing history, and performance scores
l4_steps.kpi: ≥2 approved vendors per critical part number; QSL review completed annually
l4_steps.pain_point: Single-source OEM-proprietary parts (Boeing BFE components) leave airline exposed to supply chain disruption; SAP Ariba vendor master requires manual synchronisation with AMOS parts database — discrepancies cause PO rejections

l4_steps.name: Issue RFQ or generate purchase order to vendor
l4_steps.input: Approved vendor shortlist, demand quantity, required delivery date, budget authorisation
l4_steps.output: RFQ responses evaluated and ranked, or confirmed purchase order issued in SAP
l4_steps.kpi: PO issuance within 4h of demand trigger for AOG parts; within 5 business days for routine replenishment
l4_steps.pain_point: AOG parts require emergency PO bypass of standard SAP approval workflow — manual workarounds create audit trail gaps and increase risk of duplicate orders and unapproved spend

l4_steps.name: Validate airworthiness documentation from vendor
l4_steps.input: Vendor-supplied FAA Form 8130-3 or EASA Form 1, Certificate of Conformance
l4_steps.output: Airworthiness documentation approval or rejection recorded in AMOS; non-conformances raised
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of incoming parts accompanied by valid, traceable airworthiness release documentation
l4_steps.pain_point: Counterfeit parts risk from non-OEM surplus suppliers; AMOS lacks automated verification against FAA/EASA airworthiness database — manual cross-check is time-consuming and error-prone during high-volume receiving periods

l4_steps.name: Receive shipment and verify against purchase order
l4_steps.input: Inbound shipment, purchase order, vendor packing list, airworthiness documentation
l4_steps.output: Goods receipt confirmation; quantity and part number discrepancies logged in AMOS
l4_steps.kpi: Receiving accuracy ≥99.5% (quantity and P/N match vs PO) on monthly cycle count
l4_steps.pain_point: No automated EDI integration with most parts suppliers requires manual goods receipt entry in AMOS, increasing keying errors; shipping damage from non-compliant vendor packaging not identified until unboxing

l4_steps.name: Perform incoming quality inspection on received parts
l4_steps.input: Received parts, airworthiness docs, incoming inspection checklist, part specification
l4_steps.output: Inspection serviceability tag applied (green = serviceable, red = unserviceable); AMOS inspection record
l4_steps.kpi: Incoming inspection completed within 4h for AOG-classified parts; within 48h for routine parts
l4_steps.pain_point: Inspector availability is a bottleneck during peak maintenance periods (C-check inductions); shelf-life controlled items (seals, O-rings, tyres) may expire during inspection backlog if not prioritised

l4_steps.name: Record serviceable parts into AMOS inventory
l4_steps.input: Inspection-passed part, green serviceability tag, airworthiness documents
l4_steps.output: Part record created in AMOS inventory with bin location, serial/batch number, and financial value
l4_steps.kpi: Inventory record accuracy ≥99.8% validated by quarterly AMOS cycle count
l4_steps.pain_point: Dual-entry requirement between AMOS (inventory) and SAP S/4HANA (financial asset register) for rotable parts creates reconciliation overhead; serial number capture omissions cause rotable tracking gaps during part-swap events

l4_steps.name: Store parts per specification and regulatory requirements
l4_steps.input: Part storage requirements (temperature, humidity, ESD sensitivity, hazmat classification)
l4_steps.output: Part physically located in compliant bin; AMOS bin location and storage condition record updated
l4_steps.kpi: Storage compliance audit pass rate ≥98% at monthly internal stores inspection
l4_steps.pain_point: Constrained line station stores lead to inadequate segregation of serviceable and unserviceable parts; ESD-sensitive avionics LRUs improperly stored in non-ESD zones cause latent damage not detectable at installation

l4_steps.name: Monitor shelf-life and time-controlled items for expiry
l4_steps.input: AMOS shelf-life alert reports, part batch/lot expiry dates, storage duration logs
l4_steps.output: Shelf-life exception report; near-expiry parts flagged in AMOS for priority issue or disposal
l4_steps.kpi: Zero serviceable parts issued or installed past expiry date; shelf-life compliance rate 100%
l4_steps.pain_point: AMOS shelf-life alerts require manual acknowledgement — items can expire unnoticed during high workload periods; system does not automatically quarantine parts on expiry date without manual configuration per part class

l4_steps.name: Issue parts against approved maintenance work orders
l4_steps.input: Approved work order part request, technician pick ticket, maintenance task card
l4_steps.output: Parts issued and consumption recorded against work order; AMOS inventory decremented
l4_steps.kpi: Pick accuracy ≥99.5%; parts issue turnaround <30 min for AOG work orders
l4_steps.pain_point: Approved alternate part number substitution (when requested P/N is unavailable) requires real-time engineering authority approval — delays issue when engineers are unavailable on shift, potentially extending AOG ground time

l4_steps.name: Trigger reorder when stock breaches reorder point
l4_steps.input: AMOS stock level alert (below reorder point threshold)
l4_steps.output: Purchase requisition auto-generated and transmitted to SAP Ariba for PO processing
l4_steps.kpi: Reorder trigger-to-PO issuance lead time <2 business days for routine; <4h for critical-classified parts
l4_steps.pain_point: AMOS-to-SAP Ariba integration operates on overnight batch synchronisation — same-day reorder triggers do not generate POs until next business day, requiring manual intervention for critical stock-outs

l4_steps.name: Identify and segregate unserviceable and surplus parts
l4_steps.input: Periodic inventory review output, unserviceable tags, surplus stock report from AMOS
l4_steps.output: Unserviceable and surplus parts list with recommended disposition (repair, return, or scrap)
l4_steps.kpi: Unserviceable inventory disposition completed within 90 days of unserviceable tagging
l4_steps.pain_point: Accumulation of unserviceable rotables awaiting shop repair decisions ties up significant working capital; AMOS has no automated escalation for aged unserviceable items — management visibility relies on manual report generation

l4_steps.name: Process disposal, scrap, or vendor return with credit
l4_steps.input: Disposition decision, unserviceable part, vendor return authorisation (VRA), warranty claim documentation
l4_steps.output: Credit note or scrap record; rotable asset removed from AMOS inventory and SAP asset register
l4_steps.kpi: Vendor return credit recovery ≥90% of part value for in-warranty components; scrap processing completed within 30 days of disposition decision
l4_steps.pain_point: Warranty claim processing with OEMs (Boeing, CFM) averages 45–90 days; manual credit note reconciliation between AMOS and SAP Accounts Payable leads to write-off errors and unrecovered warranty value
